chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Ayyub ibn Nuh al-Nakha'i, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far عليهما السلام, who said:
I asked him about a well into which a pigeon, a chicken, a mouse, a dog, or a cat falls. He said: “It suffices you to draw from it buckets, for that purifies it, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.”

key_terms.تَنْزَحَ: to draw out water from the well
key_terms.دِلَاءً: buckets drawn from the well for purification
key_terms.ٱلْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.ٱلْحَمَامَةُ: a pigeon falling into the well
key_terms.ٱلْفَأْرَةُ: a mouse falling into the well
key_terms.ٱلْكَلْبُ: a dog falling into the well

ai.seo_question: How is a well purified in Shia fiqh if an animal falls into it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the purification of well water after certain animals fall into it. The Imam عليه السلام states that drawing out buckets of water is sufficient to purify the well, indicating a practical fiqh ruling in matters of ritual purity.
